Happy Tuesday, **Zeteo** fans - it's **Swin** again. I've reported on how
**Donald Trump 's **second administration can be [understood primarily as
a](https://www.rollingstone.com/politics/politics-features/trump-
administration-government-employees-snitch-1235381036/) "den of snitches,
'freaks,' and paranoid tyrants." Since last year, the snitching, the
freakishness, and the paranoia and tyranny have only gotten worse - and
Trump's [disastrously unpopular bloodbath](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-iran-war-
pentagon-good-news) in the Middle East made matters
_[much](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-huge-hunt-leakers-nyt)_ worse for Team
Trump, turbo-charging the amount of leaking and ass-covering amongst the den
of freaks.

In today's '**First Draft** ,' we have another update for you on how all this
backbiting and fascist-'**Office Space** '-style governance can take some very
humorous twists and turns, at the expense of Trump himself. Also, Trump drops
his "Anti-Weaponization" slush fund - for now - and a few Democrats belatedly
discover a fraction of spine after marching with Israeli extremists.

In April, Donald Trump was so furious about leaks of highly sensitive
information to two journalists that the U.S. president - as **Zeteo** [first
reported](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-huge-hunt-leakers-nyt) - ordered senior
officials to launch a massive leak hunt throughout his government.

Trump wanted to know who had blabbed to _New York Times_ reporters Maggie
Haberman and Jonathan Swan for their forthcoming book _[Regime
Change](https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Regime-Change/Maggie-
Haberman/9781668067246)_ , including for their fly-on-the-wall [accounts
of](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/07/us/politics/trump-iran-war.html)
Trump's march to war with Iran.

By May, the president was so livid and paranoid about the leaks that he pushed
his Justice Department to seriously consider [raiding the homes of
reporters](https://zeteo.com/p/more-paranoid-trump-pushes-officials), or just
jailing them until they sold out their anonymous sources.

It's June now. Given that Trump officials had said this leak hunt was such a
**"[big deal](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-huge-hunt-leakers-nyt)"** to the
president, we wanted to check in with our well-placed sources about how the
hunt was going, as it stretches on into the summer.

In the past several weeks, it appears to have stalled out. President Trump
didn't get what he wanted, which was to very quickly see some (figurative)
heads on plates: to identify which of his trusted appointees had leaked, and
find out how he could punish them for, in Trump's repeated phrasing, such **"
treason."**
